description: A sap-sucking insect that attacks soybean and other legumes. Both adults and nymphs feed on plant sap, reducing plant growth and yield. Originally from Asia, it has become an important pest in several crop regions.
symptoms: Clusters of small brown shield-shaped insects on stems and leaves
Sticky honeydew deposits that may lead to sooty mold
favorable_conditions: Presence of kudzu plants near fields
Dense vegetation where insects can reproduce
spread: Adult insects flying to new fields
Movement from kudzu plants to nearby crops
management: Monitor fields regularly for insect clusters
Remove nearby kudzu plants when possible
Use resistant or tolerant soybean varieties
biological_control: Parasitic wasps such as Paratelenomus saccharalis
General predators like spiders and lady beetles
chemical_control: Apply when pest populations reach economic threshold
prevention: Monitor fields early in the season
Maintain field sanitation and crop rotation
